## Briefing

::: {.rq-lesson}
**Welcome to Region 2.** Real data are messy, and every later result depends on how you clean them. Read first: [Cleaning Messy Data](../r-foundations/cleaning_messy_data.qmd). You need the file **`ncd_messy`**: every question that uses it has a download button.
:::

```{r}
library(janitor)
raw <- read_csv(c("../data/ncd_messy.csv", "data/ncd_messy.csv")[file.exists(c("../data/ncd_messy.csv", "data/ncd_messy.csv"))][1], show_col_types = FALSE)
glimpse(raw)
```

::: {.rq-lesson}
**The order of work.** (1) Keep the raw file; clean a copy with a script. (2) **Look**: `glimpse()`, `count()` of each category, `range()` of each number. (3) Fix **one problem at a time** and re-check. (4) Keep a **log** of what changed and how many rows.
:::

```{r}
d <- raw |> clean_names()
count(d, sex)                                  # eight spellings of two categories
d |> mutate(sex = case_when(str_to_lower(sex) %in% c("m", "male") ~ "Male",
                            str_to_lower(sex) %in% c("f", "female") ~ "Female")) |> count(sex)
```

::: {.rq-lesson}
**Types, placeholders, duplicates.** `parse_number()` reads a number out of text such as "7.2 g" (check what still turns into `NA`). A code like **999** is a placeholder: set it to `NA` and report it, do not fill in a mean. `distinct()` removes **exact** copies; the **same ID with different values** needs a look at the source.
:::
